# Golden parity data

These files pin the Rust `tabtool-core` behavior to the Apple `TabToolKit`
implementation.

## Locales

There is one file per supported test locale:

- `en_US`
- `de_DE`
- `fr_FR`
- `zh_CN`
- `ja_JP`
- `ko_KR`

Each file contains detection, parsing, writer, sorting, filter, clipboard,
export, encoding-oracle and sort-divergence cases. The Swift generator is the
authority; do not edit these files by hand.

## Regeneration

From `app/universal`:

```
cargo run -p xtask -- golden
```

The task builds `tools/swift-golden` and runs it once per locale. From the
repository root, the direct equivalent for one locale is:

```
swift run --package-path tools/swift-golden swift-golden \
  app/universal/testdata/fixtures \
  app/universal/testdata/golden/en_US.json \
  -AppleLocale en_US -AppleLanguages '(en)'
```

`-AppleLanguages` is required in addition to `-AppleLocale`: Foundation's
localized collation follows the preferred language, while `-AppleLocale` alone
pins the locale decimal separator. Run it for `en`/`de`/`fr`/`zh`/`ja`/`ko`.

Check the committed data without Swift:

```
cargo run -p xtask -- golden --check
```

`golden --check` requires macOS. The Rust test itself is compiled only on
macOS, because the goldens record Foundation behavior.

## macOS and Foundation version caveat

The sort and filter expectations come from the Foundation/ICU version on the
machine that regenerated the files. Regenerating on a different macOS version
can change collation results. Treat a golden diff as a behavior change: inspect
it, update the Rust implementation if the difference is matchable, and record
an approved divergence otherwise.

## Known divergences

`known_divergences.json` tracks cases where Foundation and Rust deliberately
differ. Each entry has:

- `locale` — the locale identifier;
- `cells` — the one-column sort input;
- `rustOrder` — the order Rust produces;
- `reason` — why the difference is accepted.

The Foundation order is not stored in this file: each locale's golden carries
it in `sortDivergences`, generated by the Swift tool. The Rust test looks up the
matching cells there, checks that the Foundation order still differs from
`rustOrder`, and checks that both are permutations of the input. If either side
changes, the test fails so the divergence is re-evaluated rather than silently
hidden.

Sorting uses ICU4X on every platform. Known Foundation differences are tracked
here instead of being removed from the corpus.
